text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS

-- The government is expected to announce tax rises on Monday, targeting profitable businesses and well-off households first. Prime Minister Lionel Jospin holds ministerial meeting this morning on measures to curb public deficits.

-- Finance Minister Dominique Strauss Kahn confirmed to National Assembly defence committee that the state would reduce its stake in Thomson-CSF to below 50 percent from 58 percent, and planned to build around Thomson-CSF a French defence industry pillar before considering European alliances.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Valeo sales rose by 14.6 percent in the first half.
-- Thomson Multimedia expects a return to operating profit for 1997.
-- LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault presented formal offer to Guinness and GrandMet to merge the three companies' wine and spirits activities, which was greeted coldly by Guinness and GrandMet.
-- Prime Minister Lionel Jospin is said to be considering raising employers' mandatory labour contributions, and increasing the tax on corporate profits by some 10 percent.
L'AGEFI
-- Bill proposes to give co-operative status to savings banks caisses d'epargne, widen distribution of popular savings scheme Livret A.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Government considers exceptional tax on corporate profits for 1997, which is currently at 36.6 percent, and may raise tax on life-assurance contracts to five percent from 3.9 percent.
-- Association of Eurotunnel shareholders (AAE) calls for investigation into fall in share prices after shareholders approved the restructuring prospectus last week.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Government has decided not to privatise nuclear power plant builder Framatome, according to union sources.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- French government ponders sale of Thomson-CSF.
-- Renault seeks to cut costs by about 20 billion francs by the year 2000.
